text:
noah_sales: Heads up  Horizon Diagnostics (pilot) hit a surprise $11.6k overage on April invoice. Customer asking for an exception credit to avoid churn.

tia_revops: What caused the spike? billing error or load testing?

noah_sales: They ran a late-stage model bench that produced a storm of requests. They believed pilot allowance covered short bursts. Our contract doesn't explicitly exempt load tests.

rachel_finance: Can we see the invoice and token audit? @billing-bot please dump lines.

billing-bot: Invoice HOR-2026-04:\n1) API usage: $19,850\n2) Pilot credit: -$5,000\n3) Onboarding promo: -$1,250\nNet: $13,600\nClaimed overage: ~$11,600 linked to two peak days. Token audit attached to ticket BILL-3490.

tia_revops: Customer ARR estimate ~150k, strategic for med imaging integrations. They say they'll churn unless we offer relief.

rachel_finance: My discretionary goodwill cap is $6k. Anything above needs CRO/CFO sign-off. Recommend tying any credit to a short-term committed prepay.

marc_legal: If we grant >$5k we should record an exception memo and add explicit language to future SOWs about acceptance/load testing billing.

noah_sales: Customer proposes we cover $9k if they commit to a 3-month prepaid trial upgrade. They want a quick turnaround.

tia_revops: That seems reasonable to retain them. I can add a billing flag to prevent future accidental tests and require a test-notice checkbox in onboarding.

rachel_finance: I'll approve $9k conditional on a signed 3-month prepay and an exception memo filed. marc_legal to draft amendment.

marc_legal: I'll prepare amendment and exception memo, log in deal-exceptions ledger.

billing-bot: Created credit memo CM-HOR-2026-04 for $9,000. Waiting for amendment upload to apply.

noah_sales: Uploaded signed commitment at 1805030000. Please apply credit.

billing-bot: Applied credit. Updated net due: $4,600. Invoice adjusted. :white_check_mark:

rachel_finance: Approving $9k one-time credit and documenting exception. Closing thread.
